players.product: critical subsystems / weldments & cleaning services for wafer-fab equipment

quarterly_data.signal: CFO (non-GAAP): Q1 2026 total revenue of $533.7 million vs $506.6 million in the prior quarter (Products $465.7 million, Services $68 million), above the midpoint of the guided range; total gross margin 16.5% vs 16.1% on better product mix and higher volumes; operating margin 5.1%; EPS $0.31 on net income of $14.5 million. Operating cash flow was negative $33.3 million, driven primarily by higher working capital as UCT builds inventory to meet near-term demand.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $533.7 million; Products $465.7 million; Services $68 million; gross margin 16.5%; operating margin 5.1%; EPS $0.31; operating cash flow negative $33.3 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 guidance: total revenue between $565 million and $605 million and EPS in the range of $0.44-$0.60. CEO: the forecast shows close to double digits growth quarter-over-quarter from Q1 to Q2, and UCT expects a similar range of growth going forward and for the second half. CFO: gross margin slightly up in Q2 and continuing to move up toward the Q4 timeframe as revenue rises; product margins span a large bell curve from 10% to 50%-60% depending on whether it is a component part, a module or a gas panel.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $565 million to $605 million; EPS $0.44-$0.60; product margins 10% to 50%-60%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: the global footprint supports around $3 billion in revenue today and can scale up to $4 billion with modest incremental capital investment; the current run rate is still $2.2 billion, and UCT can build the capacity to reach the $4 billion run rate in six to nine months. Management does not expect infrastructure capacity to be its constraint, given progress in workforce development, strategic supply chain and operational scaling.
quarterly_data.figure: around $3 billion capacity today; up to $4 billion with modest capital; current run rate $2.2 billion; six to nine months to build

quarterly_data.signal: WFE outlook (CEO): customers are quoting $140 billion-$145 billion WFE in 2026, 18%-20% year-over-year growth, and talking about 15% and above for 2027. The fastest-growing segments (leading-edge foundry logic, HBM and advanced packaging) are etch and deposition intensive: customers see deposition and etch at mid-30s of WFE in the first half rising to the high 30s in the second half. Non-dep/etch segments are flattish; trailing-node foundry logic is flattish rather than declining.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 WFE $140 billion-$145 billion; 18%-20% growth; 15% and above for 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Demand drivers (CEO): hyperscalers and cloud providers are expected to spend around $600 billion in 2026 on data center capacity. AI capacity has been gated by memory capacity for the past three, four quarters; all the major memory customers are now investing in greenfield factories and upgrading existing fabs, which unlocks constrained capacity, and new leading-edge factory launches are seen at all three leading customers, TSMC, Intel and Samsung. Strong demand is occurring alongside emerging supply-side constraints, including clean room capacity and the time required to bring new fabs online; demand continues to build week by week and the cycle should accelerate into the second half.

China (CEO): domestic China business is less than 5% of overall revenue. China was building inventory and safety stock in 2024 and 2025, when it became 35%-40% of worldwide WFE; it is now back to normal in the low 20s% of worldwide WFE. Domestic Chinese WFE customers are gradually increasing their share within the China WFE market, a growth opportunity for UCT.
quarterly_data.figure: domestic China less than 5% of revenue; China WFE share from 35%-40% back to low 20s%

quarterly_data.signal: Services are tied to wafer starts, which are rising across IDMs and foundries on AI demand, fab expansions and higher tool utilization. Management expects double-digit growth for the year on the services side, and services to stay in a range of 10%-12% of overall revenue going forward. Growth playbook: defend the core, enter new modules and new gas panel business as customers expand their portfolios, and win at the next node inflection through NPI centers of excellence in the U.S., Europe and Asia.
quarterly_data.figure: Services double-digit growth for the year; 10%-12% of overall revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet (CFO): in February UCT priced a $600 million offering of zero coupon convertible senior notes and used part of the proceeds to fully repay its Term Loan B, reducing annual cash interest expense by approximately $30 million; after quarter end it upsized its revolving credit facility from $150 million to $250 million with maturity extended to 2031. The weighted average borrowing rate is expected to fall from around 6.2% to approximately 1.4%. CFO Sheri Savage also announced she will retire after 17 years, staying until a successor is found.
quarterly_data.figure: $600 million zero coupon convertible notes; approximately $30 million annual interest savings; revolver $150 million to $250 million; borrowing rate around 6.2% to approximately 1.4%
